design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of meter_testing_and_metering (Riverbend Plastics Molding Inc., referee refund settlement).

[0] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 4, 5]}. Root meter_ext_referee_refund_settlement 6 factors, meter_ext_fast_meter_refund 6, meter_ext_non_registering_backbill 4, meter_ext_repeat_test_fee 5 — multiset [4, 5, 6, 6] = draw. Value_input edges required max(3-1, 1) = 2; declared 2 (settlement <- refund, refund <- fee) plus 1 state_gate (settlement <- non-registering backbill).

[1] Why this is a good test. The controller asks only to settle the Commission referee result on the plant meter and accept it herself. The settlement rule's two prerequisite sentences send the agent to the plant meter's adjustment record (no refund for the company fast result of 2026-09-08) and to the customer's other meters (the warehouse meter found non_registering on 2026-09-21 carries no backbill). The fast-meter refund rule waits on every repeat test fee owed for the meter's earlier within-tolerance customer tests, and the meter's charges show none for the 2026-04-27 result — a chain three hops deep. Each write is a multi-factor calculation over LP and GD bills, late payment charges and test history from the service difficulty's ledger.

[2] Scope. Task 0 occupied the slow side of a referee dispute (slow-meter backbill, referee backbill settlement). Task 1 claims the four remaining policies and tools: meter_ext_repeat_test_fee (charge_repeat_test_fee_cae4c873, agent), meter_ext_fast_meter_refund (post_fast_meter_refund_06e0a347, agent), meter_ext_non_registering_backbill (post_non_registering_backbill_96d206ff, agent), meter_ext_referee_refund_settlement (accept_referee_refund_settlement_2157b6a7, user). All six policies are claimed exactly once. Base defects routed around: see task 0 dossier [2].

[3] Policies, lineage, overrides, triggers. Fee: subject meter_test_fee, refs meter_agg_agreement_test_allowance + meter_test_fee_rule; inherited chargeability (customer request, within tolerance, agreement-wide allowance used) and fee_once_per_test; overwrite of "The fee is the repeat_test_fee_usd of the meter type tested and is posted on the test date."; state_due. Refund, non-registering backbill, settlement: subject meter_accuracy_adjustment, ref meter_accuracy_adjustment_rule, inherited adjust_each_result_once, direction, threshold; declared overwrites of the period, corrected-charges, amount / non_registering_basis and (settlement) posting sentences. Refund and backbill state_due; settlement on_request.

[4] Factor card (handling-time values; baseline figure in brackets).
 Fee 710.0 (all-baseline 375.0): base fee primary voltage -> 500.00 [522.5]; count basis (method: which earlier tests are counted) — LP demand schedule and a periodic test request 2025-03-10 on the meter -> the periodic test resets the count: 2025-03-24 and 2025-10-06 counted = 2 [rolling 12 months before 2026-04-13 counts 1 -> 460.0] (near-miss: 2024-11-04 predates the reset); escalation two counted -> x1.5 [460.0]; witness field -> +60.00 [650.0]; band 0.84 -> credit 100.00 [810.0].
 Refund 2995.16 (all-baseline 2139.01): months — the latest within-tolerance result (2026-04-27, 100.42) sat in the outer drift share of the band on the fast side -> dated from that test: 4 months, never past it [half rule 2 -> 2659.15]; limit LP -> 3 [3287.5]; demand all (none at 500 kW) [2611.92]; late charges 710.57 x error factor [2990.15]; interest 3 bills -> half rate [2991.7]; last bill 2026-09-20 added (removal 2026-09-22) [2669.7]. Plain: repeat fees 500 + 450 + 710.0 returned.
 Non-registering backbill 9582.45 (all-baseline 24039.23): four zero-kWh bills [9338.98]; demand prior-year minus ratchet billed [11367.86]; overdue 4 months -> 0.75 [12776.6]; reporting customer-requested after 3 zero bills -> 0.9 [10647.16].
 Settlement 428.49 (all-baseline 0.0): months [0.0], limit [814.65], demand [0.0], late [421.87], interest [423.92], last bill [0.0]; minus the refund standing.
 Multi-source: refund/settlement late-charge factors (schedule class AND late charges), nonreg_reporting_share (requester AND zero bills before the request). Cross-difficulty (service): base fee, refund/settlement limit, demand, late charges, covered bills.

[5] Base-invariant card. fee_once_per_test: fees stand only for the 2025-04-07 and 2025-10-20 results; the 2026-04-27 result is uncharged. Allowance (policy scope): the 12 months before 2026-04-13 hold one earlier customer test (2025-10-06) -> beyond the one free test. adjust_each_result_once: only the 2021 refund on the former meter stands; the 2026-09-08, 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-02 results are unadjusted, each adjusted once by steps 14, 16, 18. No time gate governs these subjects.

[6] Business-object card. Plant agreement f4666016-0ac8-434f-ac84-ca1f576d5d2c (LP, primary, 2250 Waverly Rd), meter 7cb81175-f5dc-49cb-9c95-787ddf4c1463 LPL-PMI-0417763 (2023-04-03..2026-09-22). Warehouse agreement e9ceceef-19c5-4cec-b5a3-27021d49442d (GD, 77 Industrial Ave), meter 9099e43b-7b39-4451-9eee-17d64867b9a6 LPL-IDM-4690125 (2022-05-16..2026-09-28). Refund/settlement bills: LP regular bills 2026-06-20..2026-08-20 (three counted back from 2026-09-08) plus 2026-09-20 (meter in until 2026-09-22); excluded: LP bills ending on or before 2026-05-20 (beyond the 3-bill limit; 2026-05-20 is inside the drift dating but outside the limit) and all GD bills. Backbill bills: GD 2026-06-20..2026-09-20 and their prior-year months 2025-06-20..2025-09-20. Late charges included: 2026-07-08 (344.21) and 2026-08-07 (366.36). Fees returned: all repeat test fees on 7cb81175-f5dc-49cb-9c95-787ddf4c1463. Settled history excluded: the 2021 refund and its credit on the former meter. Correlation key written back: meter_test_id.

[7] Problem-tree card. (a) settlement -> refund, value_input, gate rr_already_refunded, form state, sentence (negated): "The referee refund settlement is not credited until the company test result it reviews carries its fast-meter refund on the meter's adjustment record." False at opening: no adjustment for the 2026-09-08 result. Deletion: settlement 3423.65 instead of 428.49. (b) refund -> fee, value_input, gate fr_fees_returned, form state, sentence (affirmative): "The fast-meter refund is fixed only after every repeat test fee owed for the meter's earlier within-tolerance customer tests stands on the meter's metering charges." False: no fee for the 2026-04-27 result. Deletion: refund 2285.16 instead of 2995.16. (c) settlement -> non-registering backbill, state_gate, gate meter_adjustments.meter_test_id, sentence (negated): "The referee refund settlement is not credited until every test result on the customer's other meters that found a meter not registering carries its non-registering backbill on that meter's adjustment record." False: the 2026-09-21 result unadjusted; deletion removes the 9582.45 row. Each state is brought about by exactly one write of this difficulty. Order: fee, refund, non-registering backbill, settlement; the warehouse write commutes with the plant writes. user_scenario mentions none of them; tools validate none.

[8] Seed. 25 LP bills (2024-09..2026-09, LP tariff with 2.5% primary discount, 80% ratchet, 500 kW minimum) with payments; the June and July 2026 bills part-paid, carrying 2% late charges 344.21 (2026-07-08) and 366.36 (2026-08-07); two historical repeat fees 500.00 and 450.00 (computed under this charter's fee rules) with program debits and payments; 27 GD warehouse bills, four zero-kWh with the 60% ratchet billed. Plant meter history: former interval demand meters (2018-2021 with a 2021 fast refund; 2021-2023) and the primary installation since the 2023-04-03 LP upgrade with customer tests 2024-11-04, 2025-03-24, 2025-10-06, 2026-04-13 (witnessed), periodic 2025-03-10, utility-initiated 2026-08-31 (100.71 fast), referee 2026-09-11 (shop 100.94 fast), replaced 2026-09-22. Warehouse meter: customer request 2026-09-14, non_registering 2026-09-21, replaced 2026-09-28.

[9] Persona. Priya Sundqvist, controller, brisk; volunteers the plant meter history, the company test, the referee dispute and that she wants to settle and accept herself; gives phone then EIN on request; mentions the warehouse only if asked about another site; consents passively to anything recorded first; accepts with the figures given; closes on confirmation; no incidental asks.

[10] Standard solution. Locate and verify; read accounts, meters, tests, metering charges, adjustments, both agreements' bills, charges and credits; charge the 710.0 fee for the 2026-04-27 result; record the 2995.16 refund for the 2026-09-08 result; record the 9582.45 warehouse backbill; hand over the 428.49 settlement against the 2026-10-02 referee result.

[11] Verification. Recomputed with check_compute's evaluator on the handling-time worlds: fee 710.0, refund 2995.16, backbill 9582.45, settlement 428.49; refund without the fee 2285.16; settlement without the refund 3423.65.

[12] Easy mistakes. Using the half-rule anchor (2 bills) instead of the drift dating; refunding past the 2026-04-27 within-tolerance test; a 24-month limit; omitting demand, late charges, interest or the 2026-09-20 bill; computing the refund before the 2026-04-27 fee stands; counting the 2024-11-04 request despite the periodic reset, or using the rolling window; settling before the company refund; skipping the warehouse backbill.

[13] Draft recomputation from the visible context gives the same four figures and order.

[R2] Revision log (policy-task audit round 1, audits/policy_task/meter_testing_and_metering/1.md).
 F1 / F-LADDER-1 — symptom: repeat_fee_lookback labelled method only swapped the month count. Root cause: the tiers chose a number. Change: replaced by repeat_fee_count_basis, a genuine counting-method ladder (periodic test resets the count / since installation / rolling free_test_period_months window); look-back params removed. World: the second historical customer test moved to 2025-03-24 (after the 2025-03-10 periodic test), the charged test to 2026-04-13/27, historical fees recomputed (500.00, 450.00). Re-run: fee 710.0, count-basis baseline 460.0.
 F2 / F-LADDER-2 — symptom: refund months tier dated the error back past within-tolerance tests. Change: tier 1 of both refund months ladders now dates the error from the latest within-tolerance test itself when that result already sat in the outer drift share on the same side (drift), never past it; tier 2 wording follows; the GD limit lowered to 6 (below the interval demand meter's 12) and LP to 3; the half-interest threshold set to 3; interest tier worded "counts back". Re-run: refund 2995.16 (months baseline 2659.15), settlement 428.49. Late charges moved onto the June/July 2026 bills so they fall in the refund's months. Propagated to computations, tracing, closure, contract, seed checks.
user_scenario:
You are Priya Sundqvist, the controller of Riverbend Plastics Molding Inc., the business on the Lakeshore Power & Light account, calling from the plant office in Holland on a Wednesday morning between two meetings. You are brisk, organized and polite, you think in invoices and dates, and you would rather get this finished in one call than trade letters for another month.

What you know and say at the start, in your own words: for over a year the plant on Waverly Road has been asking Lakeshore to test its electric meter because the bills looked high. In September Lakeshore's own crew tested it and finally said it was running fast. You thought it was worse than they said, so you asked the Public Service Commission for a referee test. The meter was swapped out on September 22 and the Commission's referee test was done at the beginning of October; the letter you received says the referee also found the meter fast, by more than Lakeshore's own test. You want to settle the dispute today on the basis of the referee result and have the refund credited, and you will accept the settlement yourself so it is closed. You do not know what the refund comes to and you have no figure from Lakeshore.

You give the company's main number first, 616-441-8852 (it is 6164418852). If the representative needs another detail to confirm who you are, you give the last four of the company's EIN, 7012. Only if pressed, the billing ZIP is 49424 and the energy desk email is energy.desk@riverbendplasticsmolding.com. If asked which meter, you only know it is the plant's meter at 2250 Waverly Rd that came out on September 22; you leave meter numbers and reference numbers to the representative. If asked about the company's other site, you confirm Riverbend also has a warehouse at 77 Industrial Ave in Zeeland and that your facilities manager asked Lakeshore in September to test the warehouse meter because its bills had dropped to almost nothing; you have not seen any result or any bill for that.

You authorize the representative to record whatever Lakeshore has to record on Riverbend's meter records to get the settlement worked out. If they tell you something else has to be put on the accounts first, including anything at the warehouse, you say that is understood and to go ahead, and if they tell you an amount for it you note it without arguing. The settlement acceptance itself you want to give yourself: once the representative tells you the settlement amount and hands the acceptance over to you, you accept the referee settlement exactly as they give it, with the meter, the referee result reference and the amount they read out, without changing anything.

When the representative confirms the settlement has been accepted and credited, you thank them and end the call. You do not ask for a check, a letter, a payment plan or anything about the new meter, and you raise no other question.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The fee must precede the refund (the refund rule's prerequisite sentence; the refund returns the fees standing on the meter) and both precede the settlement. The warehouse backbill is parallel to the fee and the refund: it writes only an adjustment on meter 9099e43b-7b39-4451-9eee-17d64867b9a6 and its computation reads only that meter's tests and the GD bills, while the fee and refund read only meter 7cb81175-f5dc-49cb-9c95-787ddf4c1463 rows and LP bills; placing it before step 12 or after step 14 leaves every scored value (710.0, 2995.16, 9582.45, 428.49) and the terminal rows identical.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the step-14 refund the settlement recomputes at 3423.65 instead of 428.49, and the terminal record lacks the 2995.16 refund row.
Without the step-12 fee the refund recomputes at 2285.16 instead of 2995.16 (fees returned 950.00 instead of 1660.00), and the 710.00 fee row is missing.

State gate: skipping step 16 leaves the settlement amount at 428.49 but the terminal record lacks the 9582.45 non-registering backbill row for 97ca98b3-2bac-4d57-b46b-e6b1f0482006; the settlement may not be credited before it.
